decisions.reason: As a former flagship tied closely to the firm's announced cloud-messaging direction and backed by visible prior investment, management is still inclined to justify and retain it despite weaker later website visibility.

Because it extends the firm's document workflow capabilities and likely reuses existing technology and customer relationships, management would tend to continue with it while interpreting modest traction as a portfolio-positioning issue rather than a clear failure.

Its lower visibility, narrower strategic importance, and more legacy character make it harder by 2022 to defend continued commitment versus reallocating resources to stronger cloud and security developments.

Threat protection remains highly consistent with the firm's secure and compliant value proposition, so sunk development costs and reputational commitment support ongoing retention even if it is no longer prominently marketed.

Although related to the core email-security offer, its limited public prominence and likely overlap with broader protection services make management more willing by now to rationalize the portfolio and move resources elsewhere.
